source_note: Printhead lineup and drive principles compiled from Brinter public product material and press coverage (2021-2022). Bore sizes, pressure ranges and speeds are NOT included because they are configuration- and consumable-dependent and were not published in a form worth copying. The questionnaire asks for them; it does not assume them. MAINTAINER NOTE: this repository is published by Brinter AM Technologies Oy, so this profile can and should be replaced with authoritative figures from the product documentation rather than remaining a compilation of public sources. Until that happens it stays marked as compiled, because saying otherwise would be the exact overclaim this project exists to prevent.
platform_notes: Modular: one printhead mounted at a time, tool-free semi-automatic change, heads swap between Brinter products.
Native workflow is STL into a browser-based slicer, out as G-code. This integrator wraps that same STL with its dossier rather than replacing the slicer.
A disinfecting blue-light module is available; if used, record it under sterility_method.

printheads.name: Pneuma Tool
printheads.suits: general-purpose extrusion of hydrogels and pastes

printheads.name: Pneuma Cooled
printheads.suits: low to medium viscosity hydrogels, silicones and pastes such as collagen or Matrigel
prompts: cartridge_temp is a cooling setpoint here; record the value actually held, not the dial.

printheads.name: Pneuma Pro
printheads.suits: low to medium viscosity hydrogels with living cells at +37 C

printheads.name: Visco Tool
printheads.principle: screw-driven mechanical extrusion, endless piston pump
printheads.suits: viscous pastes where a displacement drive gives better repeatability than pressure
prompts: A progressive-cavity drive delivers a constant volume per revolution, so the controlled variable is a volume rate and a screw speed, NOT a pressure. Rule P0 will ask for volumetric_flow_rate and screw_speed.

printheads.name: Visco Bio
printheads.suits: medical-grade materials where dead volume and cross-contamination matter
prompts: Near-zero dead volume and one cartridge per material. If you are relying on single-cartridge-per-material to avoid cross-contamination, record it: it is a GMP-relevant control, not a convenience.
Programmable suck-back affects start and end points of every strand. Record the suck-back setting under an x- parameter if your acceptance criteria depend on strand ends.

printheads.name: Rotary Tool
printheads.principle: screw-driven mechanical extrusion, endless piston pump

printheads.name: Droplet Tool / MicroDroplet Tool
printheads.principle: electromagnetically actuated microvalve droplet dispensing, solenoid driven
printheads.suits: droplet deposition of low-viscosity fluids and cell suspensions

printheads.name: Granu Tool
printheads.suits: thermoplastic granules, or a thermoplastic binder mixed with powder fillers
prompts: Barrel and nozzle can be heated to +250 C. If this head is running in the same build as a cell-laden head, record the thermal separation: a cartridge_temp of 200 C next to a cell-laden strand is a viability question, not just a process setting.

printheads.name: Multi-fluidic printing tool
printheads.principle: digital multifluidic, many material combinations from one head
prompts: This head can produce many material combinations in a single build. The format expects each distinct formulation to be its own <b:bioink>, so a build using N combinations needs N entries, not one entry with a range.

defaults.sterility_prompt: If the blue-light disinfection module was used, record it in sterility_method rather than leaving the field as aseptic-assembly.
